bib.title: Character-Level Language Modeling with Deeper Self-Attention

question: Can a deep non-recurrent transformer with fixed context beat RNN variants at character-level language modeling?
hypothesis: The transformer's ability to quickly propagate information over arbitrary distances suits long-sequence character modeling, and auxiliary losses make very deep (64-layer) training feasible.
contributions: 64-layer causal character transformer trained without state passed between batches, state of the art on text8 and enwik8
Three auxiliary losses (intermediate positions, intermediate layers, multiple targets) plus per-layer learned positional embeddings
Ablations and qualitative analysis of long-range copying

method.summary: A 64-layer causal transformer reads 512-byte windows sampled at random positions, with auxiliary losses at all positions, all layers (decayed) and two-step-ahead targets. Trained on text8 and enwik8, with extra runs on lm1b and enwik9.

datasets.name: text8
datasets.preprocessing: 27-char vocab (a-z, space); digits spelled out; non-[a-zA-Z] to a space; lowercased

datasets.name: enwik8
datasets.preprocessing: unprocessed Wikipedia text with markup, 205 unique bytes

datasets.name: lm1b
datasets.split: standard train/test split; heldout shard 01 as dev, shard 00 as test
datasets.preprocessing: preprocessed corpus with OOV words replaced by UNK

models.name: T64
models.architecture: causal transformer, per-layer learned positional embeddings

training.objective: next-byte cross-entropy at all positions in all layers plus second-target loss (weight 0.5), intermediate-layer losses dropped on a schedule
training.dropout: 0.55 in attention and ReLU layers (T64); 0.2 T12; 0.1 enwik9; 0 on lm1b
training.regularisation: dropout; auxiliary losses hypothesised as regulariser

other.intermediate_layer_schedule: layer l stops contributing after l/(2n) of training; every 62.5K steps (=4M x 1/(2*64)) the next layer's loss is dropped; only final layer after halfway
other.checkpoint_selection: best validation bpc, checked roughly every 10,000 steps

inference.decoding: scoring: final position of final layer given 512 characters, no state passed; generation by sampling
inference.prompting: seed text from enwik9 dev set

other.word_completion_cutoff: stop at space or cumulative probability below 0.001

metrics.name: bits per character (bpc)
metrics.definition: negative log2 probability of target per character; for enwik8 reported as bits per byte

metrics.name: word perplexity (lm1b)
metrics.definition: ppl = 2^(bpb*826189/159658), 826,189 bytes and 159,658 tokens in test set

eval.protocol: single run per configuration, best dev checkpoint; ablations reuse best-model hyperparameters on text8 dev

availability.code: inferred: builds on tensor2tensor library (link given); no release of this model stated

limits: Evaluation needs the full 512-character context recomputed per character, so inference is expensive
Byte-level model trails a word-level model on lm1b (40.6 vs 23.7 ppl); authors call it a starting point
Learned positional embeddings only usable because no longer contexts are needed
Single runs, no seeds or variance; ablations reuse best-model hyperparameters without retuning
Model is 5x larger than prior baselines, so comparison is not parameter-matched; T12 added for that
Compute beyond TPU v2 hours not stated; no code release stated
